name: San Andreas fault zone, Parkfield section, Central California

fault_trace.comment: Real mapped trace, San Andreas fault zone Parkfield section, from CA GIS GeoscientificInformation/Fault_Lines/MapServer/3, fetched 2026-07-03. Most heavily instrumented fault section in the world (site of the 1985-1993 Parkfield Earthquake Prediction Experiment -- a documented FAILED point-prediction attempt, directly relevant to this project's design requirements R1-R4).

gnss.fault_azimuth_comment: PCA strike of the real trace

state.recurrence_source: Historical M~6 characteristic-earthquake sequence: 1857, 1881, 1901, 1922, 1934, 1966, 2004-09-28 (the famous ~22yr average recurrence that motivated the 1985-1993 USGS Parkfield Earthquake Prediction Experiment -- which failed to predict the actual 2004 event within its forecast window, a well-documented case study). T_rec=22yr, last event 2004 -> ~22yr elapsed as of 2026 (right at the historical average, characteristically 'due').

etas_lite.target_mag_comment: Lower than SJC/Mojave (4.5) -- Parkfield's characteristic events are ~M6, but the corridor is small (15km) and 4.5+ events are too rare here in the catalog window alone; 3.5 trades operational relevance for event count, a deliberate documented choice per cluster_archetypes.py's own caveat about this tradeoff.
